voz-a-texto.title: Speech to Text
voz-a-texto.description: Dictate with your voice and watch the text appear live on screen. Free, no account. Your browser does the recognition; SonhoLab doesn't receive your voice or the text.
voz-a-texto.cta: Need voice dictation built into your own app or system? We can build that integration for you.
voz-a-texto.seoTitle: Free Speech to Text in Your Browser | SonhoLab
voz-a-texto.seoDescription: Dictate and watch the text appear live in Chrome or Edge. Free, no account. SonhoLab never receives your voice; your browser may send it to its provider.
voz-a-texto.intro: Typing out a WhatsApp message, a quick class note, or a paragraph for work isn't the only option anymore. Here you speak into your microphone and the text appears on screen as you talk, ready to copy or download as a text file. The tool uses the speech recognition already built into your browser: SonhoLab doesn't receive or store your voice or the text, but depending on the browser (in Chrome, Google) the audio may be sent to its developer's speech recognition service to be transcribed, so an internet connection is needed. It works best in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.
voz-a-texto.stepsHeading: How to turn your voice into text in 3 steps
voz-a-texto.step1Text: Click Record and your browser will ask for microphone permission the first time. Grant it once, and the tool is ready to use instantly every time you come back.
voz-a-texto.step2Text: Dictate your message, note, or paragraph at a normal pace. The text appears as you talk: what's still being processed shows in gray, and confirmed text shows in solid black. It won't be perfectly accurate every time, especially with background noise or technical vocabulary, but it still saves a lot of time compared to typing everything out.
voz-a-texto.step3Text: Press Stop when you're done talking. Then copy the text to your clipboard to paste it wherever you need, or download it straight away as a .txt file.
voz-a-texto.useCase1: Someone is driving or has their hands full cooking and needs to dictate a WhatsApp message or an email without stopping what they're doing.
voz-a-texto.useCase2: A student jots down quick notes during a lecture or meeting by speaking quietly, instead of typing frantically and missing parts of the explanation, then tidies them up later.
voz-a-texto.useCase3: Someone with a hand injury, or who simply thinks and talks faster than they type, drafts an entire document by dictating instead of typing every word.
voz-a-texto.faq1q: Does it work in every browser?
voz-a-texto.faq1a: Not equally in all of them. It works well in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge, which have solid support for the browser's built-in speech recognition. Safari and Firefox have limited or no support at all, so if you talk and nothing shows up, try opening the tool in Chrome or Edge instead.
voz-a-texto.faq2q: Can I upload an audio file or a WhatsApp voice note to transcribe it?
voz-a-texto.faq2a: No. This tool only transcribes what you say live into the microphone; it doesn't accept audio files like an MP3 or an already-recorded voice note. If you need to transcribe an existing audio file, this isn't the right tool for that job.
voz-a-texto.faq3q: Are my voice and the text sent to or stored on a server?
voz-a-texto.faq3a: Not by us: we don't receive, store, or send your voice or the text to our servers, and the text only appears on your screen. But the recognition is done by your browser, and depending on which one you use (in Chrome, Google), the audio may be sent to its developer's speech recognition service to be transcribed. That's why the tool needs internet, and why that provider's privacy policy applies to that part. If you don't want something to go through that service, don't dictate it: avoid passwords and sensitive data. Nothing is saved on this page: close the tab and it's gone, except for whatever you already copied or downloaded.
voz-a-texto.faq4q: Do I need to install anything or create an account?
voz-a-texto.faq4a: No. It runs directly in whatever browser you already have, with nothing to install and no extensions to add, and no sign-up or email required. The only thing it asks for is microphone permission, and only the first time.
voz-a-texto.faq5q: What language does it recognize when I speak?
voz-a-texto.faq5a: It recognizes whatever language the site is currently set to: if you're viewing the page in English it understands English, and the same goes if you switch it to Spanish, French, or Portuguese. Change the site's language first if you need to dictate in a different one.
